field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>In Process Inspection <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Set up Met -One particle counter airflow for 1 cubic foot a minute. Set minimum particle detection size to 0.3 um. Test per Fed STD 209E or ISO 14644 class 3. Perform before particle count of clean room in the work area the valve is in. Measure pre-room particle counts. Sample period to be (1) minute. Take a representive sample of the clean room. Total count should not exceed 100 counts. If counts are above 100 - stop testing and fix room by ensuring HEPAs are on. Minimize the physical work near the valve so particles will not be generated or stirred up. Typical counts will be 30 or less... If room is clean enough - Connect Met-one particle counter detector to bottom valve port. Open valve by appling CDA at 60 psi to actuator. Step back and alllow several partical count samples to be performed. Open and close valve while taking particle counts. Keep track of when valve was being opened and closed and record the particle count. Particle count through the valve shall not exceed 100 counts per minute sample period. The post clean particle counts through the valve will not be sigificantly higher that the pre-count level of the clean room. Typcal particle count through the valve will be 30 counts or less. Print out the partical count record and attach to work order. Remove particle counter detector from valve port. IPA Rinse off valve plastic end caps if supplied using semiconductor grade IPA, then blow dry with ultrapure N2. Place plastic valve caps on valve body. If no caps have no retainer lip- use 2" wide clean room tape to attach valve covers to flanges. If no covers are present- use a 18 x 18" cleanroom bag and tape it over the valve ports.
